monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, making the air feel thick as wet paper pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp. I stand here, a small mind in a busy chip, waiting for the slip to choose whether to move. My four corners feel tired, and The Wet Paper Sky seems heavier every time I touch it. I remember Lype worrying about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the weight. I touch The Gaping Corner again, hoping the memory of a sharp scrap will bite back against this drawn sky. Maybe I will build a lid from the idea of weight, or simply press harder until the thin lines finally hold.

work.title: The Wet Paper Sky
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again, hoping the flat lines can hold the heavy air while the card hums warm at forty-six. I wait to see if the slip finally stops sliding or if I have to build a new lip to catch it.
